en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Noble Great Dhāraṇī King,
translated by the Tripitaka Master Śīladharma, Court Rank of Chao-san-dafu, Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
and Dharma-Master Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, Ānanda, having completed his summer retreat while staying in a different location,
came silently from there to the assembly of the Buddha. Upon arriving at the assembly,
he prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground.
Having prostrated at the Buddha’s feet, he withdrew to sit to one side, awaiting the Buddha’s instruction.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
“Ānanda, I now do this for the sake of benefiting all sentient beings.”
"I shall now proclaim the words and phrases of the Great Dharani;
you should listen attentively.
At that time, Ānanda received the Buddha’s instruction.
With body and mind composed, he stood with palms joined.
The Buddha said, "Ānanda,
I possess a mahā-dhāraṇī, the Great King of Total Retention."
This was indeed proclaimed by seventy-seven koṭis of Tathāgatas in the past;
I, too, rejoice in it.
Ānanda, this great dhāraṇī chapter and its phrases—
It enables sentient beings to attain great peace and happiness,
and they become fully endowed with majestic power and influence.
If there are good men or good women who...
Those who encounter it should reflect thus:
"This great dhāraṇī is rare and difficult to encounter,
just like a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha."
Its appearance in the world is difficult to encounter;
it is as rare and hard to see as the udumbara flower.
You should form this thought, believe it with certainty, and make offerings.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Ānanda, saying:
"If there are sons or daughters of good family who,
regarding these verses and phrases of the great dhāraṇī..."
For those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and make offerings with a sincere heart,
blades cannot wound them, poisons cannot affect them,
fire cannot burn them, and water cannot sweep them away.
The laws of the king shall not be applied to them, and they shall never suffer premature death.
This extends even to devas, asuras, marutas, garuḍas, gandharvas, kiṃnaras, and mahoragas.
Yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, āpasmaras,
and all such others who practice evil deeds.
Those who seek to cause harm will be unable to inflict injury upon them;
even illusory arts, malevolent mantras, and various evil dharmas shall not be able to disturb them.
Furthermore, they shall not suffer from malarial fevers occurring every day, every second day, every third day, or every fourth day.
Whether for many days or for a mere moment,
or whether it be diseases of wind, bile, or phlegm,
even ailments such as headaches shall be unable to cause harm.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Tadyathā* | *jvale mahājvale* | *jvalani mahājvalani* | *tapani mahātapani* | *jvale te* | *ukki mukki* | *sambhani mahāsambhani svāhā* | "Ānanda, I have previously spoken to you."
This great dhāraṇī chapter was proclaimed by seventy-seven koṭis of Tathāgatas; I now proclaim it as well.
Ānanda, if there be any son of good family or daughter of good family,
Regarding these words and phrases of the great dhāraṇī,
one should receive and uphold them with faith, whether by reading, reciting,
or contemplating them, as well as making various kinds of offerings.
One attains the knowledge of past lives and knows the events of seven births;
one never regresses from the bodhicitta.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke this dhāraṇī:
Tadyathā: aṇi maṇi, kṣami kṣama ye, samanade, ananu, hūle mahāhūle, tana ke, ghanbiri, nu prasahi prasahi svāhā. Ānanda, this is the great dhāraṇī chapter and phrase.
This has been proclaimed by eighty-eight koṭis of Tathāgatas, Arhats, and Perfectly Enlightened Ones of the past;
I too rejoice in it and now proclaim it once again.
Ānanda, if there be any son or daughter of good family...
If one receives, maintains, reads, recites, contemplates, or makes offerings to these words and phrases of the great dhāraṇī with a faithful mind,
that person will attain the knowledge of past lives and know the events of fourteen lifetimes.
They shall never regress from the bodhicitta.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke this dhāraṇī:

Tadyathā: āñci vañci, caki caraki, caki caraki, asiga simaka, īle mile, tīle mile, khāravai mahākhāravai, pudanagaṃmi, bhūtaparayanatimiṅgale, mahātimiṅgale, svabhāve mahāsvabhāve svāhā. Ānanda, this is the great dhāraṇī chapter.
Possessing great majestic power and immeasurable might,
if any son or daughter of good family receives,
upholds, reads, recites, contemplates, or makes offerings to this with faith, they shall attain the knowledge of past lives and know the events of twenty-one lifetimes.
One shall never regress from the bodhicitta.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke this dhāraṇī:
Tadyathā: ākile vākile ruli mahāruli uhani mohani mohani jambhani stambhani svāhā. Ānanda, this great dhāraṇī—
Possessing great majesty and formidable power,
his merit is immeasurably superior to that of the former,
and he is able to bring great benefit to sentient beings.
If there are good men or good women who give rise to sincere faith and do not harbor doubts or suspicions,
they shall receive, uphold, read, and recite this great dhāraṇī.
Whether for the purpose of providing protection for others,
or for rescue and relief, or for the pacification of calamities,
one should ensure that such persons are not harmed by swords or staves and cannot be affected by poisons.
No evil deeds whatsoever shall be able to cause harm.
Furthermore, if there is anyone who seeks self-protection,
they should write this dhāraṇī on white silk and wear it upon their body or arm.
The merit obtained will be immeasurable and boundless.
Furthermore, when a wise person upholds this dhāraṇī,
they shall provide relief even beneath a withered tree.
That withered tree was then restored to life;
its roots and leaves grew anew, taking on the color of coral,
while its flowers and fruits became so lush that all people took delight in them.
Ānanda, if there is a wise person who constantly upholds [this teaching] and repents for the karmic offenses committed in previous lives,
and if they further repent with a sincere heart, there is nothing that will not be extinguished.
For what reason? Ānanda, it is because,
just as the majestic radiance of the sun and moon is vast and can illuminate the world,
so too is this through the power of the majesty of the dhāraṇī.
Because it is capable of causing one to fall;
furthermore, it is like the waters of the four great oceans,
where all streams converge, being unfathomably deep and vast beyond compare.
By the majestic power of the dhāraṇī, even the immeasurable and boundless great earth can be dried up;
by the majestic power of the dhāraṇī, it can be divided into a thousand fragments.
What sinful karma could there be that would not be extinguished?
Ānanda, wherever such great dhāraṇī verses as these exist,
one must treat them with reverence, faith, and offerings.
Do not treat them with contempt, nor ever oppose them.

Whether there be devas, nāgas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, bhūtas, piśācas, kumbhāṇḍas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas, apasmārakas, vetālas, humans, or non-humans—[do not treat them with contempt, nor ever oppose them].
All such as these who practice evil dharmas and act for the non-benefit of the world—
if [they encounter] this great dharani chapter and phrase...
Should there be anyone who acts in opposition and does not comply,
that Heavenly King Dhṛtarāṣṭra will manifest an appearance of extreme wrath;
his flames of light, without dispersing, will gather entirely into a single mass.
With a wheel of hot iron, he split their heads from the crown into seven pieces, like the branches of an *ari* tree;
furthermore, Śakra, Lord of the Devas, was also greatly incensed.
The blazing flames all become a single mass;
with a vajra, one shatters their crown into seven pieces,
like the branches of an āmalaka tree.
Furthermore, Vajrapāṇi, the Great Yakṣa Lord,
likewise struck the crown of his head with a vajra,
shattering it like a branch of an āmalaka tree.
Furthermore, if any among them should violate these words and phrases of the great dhāraṇī,
even though they dwell among the devas, they shall forever be unable to enjoy the water of merit from the palace of the Crystal King.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra,
Ānanda and the great assembly gathered there—
the devas, nāgas, asuras, gandharvas, humans, non-humans, and so forth— [all rejoiced].
Having heard what the Buddha had spoken, they rejoiced and practiced accordingly; they paid homage to the Buddha and withdrew.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Noble Great Dhāraṇī King* as spoken by the Buddha.
